title: Breaking down the jargon for you guys, Meta Ads doesn't need to be as...
description: Breaking down the jargon for you guys, Meta Ads doesn't need to be as complicated as some people make it out to be. Save this to avoid the confusion 😵‍💫
transcript: Meta flew me out to Silicon Valley and I've just been in the room with over 1,000 advertisers that spend tens of billions on meta ads every year. I've heard lots of jargon, so today I'm gonna break it down for you and explain what it actually means. Let's start with ROAS, which is return on ad spend, and that simply measures what you spent on ads versus what you've got in back. Incrementality is measuring what your ads produced for your business that you would not have got if you weren't running ads in the first place. The incrementality is the uplift. Ppm, which is cost per thousand impressions. It's the metric that's typically used to measure the cost of advertising. If you were to compare advertising platforms or different locations, you would use CPM. CTR stands for click through rate, which measures the percentage of people that clicked on your ad versus the people that saw it. For meta ads, a good click through rate would typically be something above 1%. If you get above 2%, you're normally doing really well. CPC stands for cost per click and measures simply how much are you paying per click on your ad. Retargeting, which is putting ads in front of people that have already interacted with your business, could be people that have visited your website, could be people on an email list, could even be people that have purchased from you previously. CAC stands for cost to acquire a Customer. One of the most important metrics in paid advertising, honestly, in all of marketing, AOV, is average order value. When people come through to your website and they purchase. The higher AOV, the better.
